newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp - EMU delay would fuel stability doubt.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp - EMU delay would fuel stability doubt.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Tuesday that delaying Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) project would raise doubts on commitment to stability in the potential euro zone.

In the text of a speech to be delivered at a seminar later today, Krupp also said that it was important that EMU would start on time, even if only a limited number of countries could take part at the initial stage.

"A delayed timetable, which is not provided for in the (Maastricht) treaty and thus would need to be ratified by all EU states, could fuel doubt on the further commitment to stability in other European countries and eventually on the realisation of currency union itself," Krupp said.
The consequences of such doubts would be an appreciation of the deutschemark and job losses, he warned.
"Germany must thus be interested in having currency union start punctually on January 1 1999, even if only a limited group of participants can belong at the beginning," Krupp said.

Krupp, also president of the regional state central bank of Hamburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Schleswig-Holstein, reaffirmed his view that an on-the-spot fulfilment of convergence criteria for monetary union was not essential.

The success of currency union would depend on the ability of a sufficient number of countries being able to meet EMU goals on inflation, interest rates and exchange rates "in a narrower sense", he said.

However the decision as to whether a country had fulfiled the deficit goal, for which the Maastricht Treaty sets a threshold of three percent of gross domestic product, would depend on a judgement on its overall economic picture.
"For good economic reasons ... the treaty is not about simply reaching numeric values," Krupp said.
